To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
graphene–WO3 composite thin-film sensors show an enhanced response for NO2 at room temperature as compared to pure WO3 thin-film sensors.
we have developed a simple approach for the synthesis of graphene–WOx nanocomposites, which were used for the first time for NO2 sensing.
we have demonstrated the preparation of graphene-based nanocomposites with WO3 and the sensing properties of the prepared nanocomposite thin films.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of graphene-based nanocomposite sensors for NO2 detection.
the development of a novel and efficient NO2 sensor.
the development of a simple, fast and reliable method for the detection of toxic NO2 at room temperature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the graphene–WO 3 nanocomposite sensor exhibits a faster response to NO2 as compared to a WO3 thin film sensor.
the response of the sensor was improved due to the synergistic effect of graphene and WO3, where the graphene acts as an electron reservoir and WO3 as an active material for the detection of gas.
the graphene–WOx nanocomposite thin layer sensor showed a better response and a faster response to NO2 than the pure WO3 thin-layer sensor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
graphene–WO3 composites are promising materials for gas sensor application.
the addition of graphene to WO3 enhances the gas sensing properties.
the addition of graphene to the WO3 layer increases the response of NO2 and decreases the response of CO2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the response of the sensor to NO2 can be improved significantly by the addition of a small amount of graphene in the WO3 layer.
a small amount of graphene in the composite can enhance the gas sensing properties of WO3.
the graphene–WOx nanocomposite layer can be used as a sensitive layer in gas sensors, which can detect NO2 at low temperatures.
